notes: Cross-cultural coverage is insufficient, so this company should get the automated second look using Alcon's Social Impact and Sustainability Report, which Item 4.D says is published on the company website. Training for eye care professionals (about 45 training centers, programs for practitioners, students and residents) is real external training, but the filing describes it as part of marketing and sales and calls it marketing activities targeted at healthcare professionals. It was therefore scored as customer education under the trap and not credited at level 3. The Legion system, an affordable phaco system for developing markets, aims at health access and affordability rather than cross-cultural inclusion, so it was not scored; being torn, the lower level was chosen. Alcon Seed Fund portfolio investments (16 projects) are framed as Alcon's own innovation strategy and tagged own_innovation. Trap terms ignored: 'chip design', 'optical design', 'licensing and collaboration opportunities' (business development deals), 'equity' (shares), 'state-of-the-art'. The Health Care Fraud section describes legal risks only, with no findings.
flags: coverage insufficient (cross_cultural); second look: no standalone report found
